# Part I: R Basics {.unnumbered}

This part teaches the R language itself. It assumes no knowledge of programming. We start with R as a calculator, and move step by step to objects, subsetting, functions, pipes, control statements and functional programming. These chapters build on one another, so read them in order.

The examples here are small, but they are chosen with audit in mind. Along the way you will meet the traps that cause most errors in audit analysis: an amount read as text, an account number that loses its leading zero, a total that silently becomes `NA`, or decimals that do not compare as equal.

The chapters in this part are:

- @sec-basics, values, vectors, data frames and the basic types of data.
- @sec-subset, picking out the elements, rows and columns you need.
- @sec-func, using and writing functions.
- @sec-basefuns, a reference of the most useful built-in functions.
- @sec-pipes, writing a chain of steps that reads like the audit procedure.
- @sec-control, `if`, `else` and loops.
- @sec-fp, applying one function to many items, with the apply family and purrr.
